title: Rational Functions and Asymptotes
seo_title: Rational Functions and Asymptotes Worksheet (Precalculus) | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Graph rational functions, identifying zeros and asymptotes when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.
meta_desc: Free precalculus worksheet on rational functions: vertical, horizontal and slant asymptotes, holes, intercepts, domain, graphs and models. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Factor first: cancelled factors are holes, the rest of the denominator's zeros are asymptotes.
key_sub: Compare degrees to find the horizontal or slant asymptote.
body_html:
How it works

  • Factor the numerator and denominator first. A factor that cancels makes a hole. A zero of the denominator that does not cancel is a vertical asymptote.
  • Horizontal asymptote: compare degrees. Top degree smaller: y = 0. Equal degrees: y = ratio of the leading coefficients. Top degree one larger: a slant asymptote from division.
  • x-intercepts come from the zeros of the numerator; the y-intercept is f(0).
  • For f(x) = a/(x − h) + k, the asymptotes are x = h and y = k.
Example

Find the asymptotes and holes of f(x) = (x − 2)(x + 1)(x − 2)(x − 3).

(x − 2) cancels: hole at x = 2

Vertical asymptote: x = 3

Degrees are equal: y = 1 ÷ 1 = 1

Answer: hole at x = 2, x = 3, y = 1

Example

Find the slant asymptote of f(x) = x² + 3x + 1x − 1.

Divide: x² + 3x + 1 ÷ (x − 1) = x + 4, remainder 5

Answer: y = x + 4

Common mistakes

  • Calling a cancelled factor an asymptote. It is a hole.
  • Using the zeros of the numerator as vertical asymptotes. They are x-intercepts.
  • Using the constant terms for the horizontal asymptote. Use the leading coefficients.
  • Shifting the wrong way: x − 3 in the denominator gives the asymptote x = 3, not −3.

faq.q: How do you find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function?
faq.a: Factor and cancel common factors. The zeros of the denominator that remain are vertical asymptotes; cancelled factors give holes.

faq.q: How do you find the horizontal asymptote?
faq.a: Compare degrees. If the numerator has the lower degree, it is y = 0. If the degrees are equal, divide the leading coefficients. If the numerator's degree is one higher, there is a slant asymptote instead.

faq.q: What is a hole in a graph?
faq.a: A single missing point where a factor cancels from the numerator and denominator.

faq.q: What does a horizontal asymptote mean in a real problem?
faq.a: It is the long-run value, such as the average cost per item approaching the cost to make one item.

items.q: What are the vertical asymptotes of f(x) = x − 6(x + 3)(x − 1)?
items.e: The denominator is (x + 3)(x − 1), which is 0 at x = −3 and x = 1. The numerator is not 0 there, so the asymptotes are x = −3 and x = 1.

items.q: Where is the hole in the graph of f(x) = x − 1x² − 4x + 3?
items.e: (x − 1) cancels, so there is a hole at x = 1. The simplified function is 1/(x − 3); at x = 1 it is −12. The hole is (1, −12).

items.q: A printer charges $5,000 to set up and $3 per poster. The average cost per poster is A(x) = (5,000 + 3x) / x. What value does the average cost approach as the number of posters gets very large?
items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = 3 ÷ 1 = 3: the setup cost is shared by more and more posters. $3.

items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = 12 ÷ 1 = 12: the setup cost is shared by more and more posters. $12.

items.e: Compare the leading coefficients: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5. Over time the tank fills with the incoming mixture. 1.5 g per liter.
